questions.question:
The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025 aims to:

I. Abolish Waqf board completely

II. streamline the management of Waqf properties
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025** aims to **streamline the management of Waqf properties**, ensuring their better utilization and preventing misuse. 
• The bill seeks to bring transparency and accountability to the administration of **Waqf boards**, which are responsible for managing properties dedicated for religious or charitable purposes under Islamic law. 
• Statement I, which suggests the complete abolition of Waqf boards, is **incorrect**. The bill does not propose eliminating Waqf boards but rather focuses on enhancing their functioning. 
• Statement II, which emphasizes streamlining the management of Waqf properties, is **correct**, as the bill is designed to address inefficiencies and corruption within the current system. 
• The correct option is **Only II**, as the primary objective of the amendment is improving the operational framework of Waqf boards without abolishing them. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Waqf:** 
• A **Waqf** is an endowment made by a Muslim for charitable or religious purposes, including properties such as mosques, schools, or orphanages. 
• Waqf properties are managed by **Waqf boards**, which are established under the Waqf Act. 
• India has a significant number of Waqf properties, with an estimated 6 lakh registered properties. 
• **Waqf Act:** 
• The **Waqf Act, 1995**, governs the administration of Waqf properties in India. The act provides mechanisms for registration, monitoring, and utilization of Waqf properties. 
• State Waqf boards are established under this act to oversee the management of Waqf properties at the state level. 
• **Issues with Waqf Management:** 
• There have been concerns over **corruption**, **mismanagement**, and **encroachment** of Waqf properties. 
• Lack of transparency and accountability has hindered the effective use of Waqf properties for their intended purposes. 
• **Key Features of the Amendment Bill:** 
• The bill seeks to enhance transparency by mandating **digital records** of Waqf properties. 
• It proposes stricter penalties for encroachment or misuse of Waqf properties. 
• The amendment emphasizes **improved oversight** by state and central governments to ensure better governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Background:** 
• Waqf properties have historically played a crucial role in supporting **education**, **healthcare**, and **community welfare**. 
• The government periodically amends the Waqf Act to address emerging challenges and improve management practices. 
• **Global Context:** 
• Similar systems of endowments, like **trusts** and **foundations**, exist in other countries to manage properties for charitable purposes. 
• Countries such as **Turkey** and **Saudi Arabia** have well-developed frameworks for managing Waqf properties. 
• **Legal Framework in India:** 
• The Constitution of India provides provisions for protecting religious and charitable endowments under **Article 26**. 
• Waqf boards are recognized as statutory bodies under the **Waqf Act**. 
• **Proposed Benefits:** 
• The amendment aims to ensure better utilization of Waqf properties for **socio-economic development**. 
• It seeks to protect Waqf properties from **encroachment** and ensure their intended use for religious and charitable purposes. </ul

questions.question: The Export Preparedness Index India is developed by ______.

options.text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Export Preparedness Index (EPI)** is developed by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the **Institute of Competitiveness**.
 
• The EPI aims to identify challenges and opportunities, enhance the effectiveness of government policies, and promote a facilitative regulatory framework for export growth in India.
 
• The first edition of the Export Preparedness Index was released in **August 2020**, and it aims to rank states and union territories based on their export performance and export ecosystem.
 
• The EPI evaluates states on four pillars: **Policy, Business Ecosystem, Export Ecosystem, and Export Performance**.
 
• **Gujarat** emerged as the top-performing state in the first edition of the EPI, followed by **Maharashtra** and **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog:**

 
 
• **NITI Aayog** stands for **National Institution for Transforming India**.
 
• It was established in **2015** as a policy think tank of the Government of India, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• The organization provides strategic and technical advice to the central and state governments.
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on fostering cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states.
 
 
 
• **Export Preparedness Index (EPI) Pillars:**
 
 
• **Policy:** Examines export-related policies at the state level to support exports.
 
• **Business Ecosystem:** Evaluates the ease of doing business in a state to promote exports.
 
• **Export Ecosystem:** Analyzes the export-related infrastructure and trade support available in a state.
 
• **Export Performance:** Measures the actual export performance of the states and union territories.
 
 
 
• **Significance of EPI:**
 
 
• Helps identify strengths and weaknesses of the export ecosystem at the state level.
 
• Encourages healthy competition among states and union territories to improve their export ecosystem.
 
• Provides a comprehensive framework to policymakers for boosting exports.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Indices by NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• **India Innovation Index:** Measures innovation performance of states and union territories.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index:** Tracks the progress of states and UTs toward achieving SDGs.
 
• **Health Index:** Evaluates the performance of states in the health sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Export Preparedness Index** is India's first comprehensive tool for ranking states and union territories on their export performance and readiness.
 
• It encourages state-level initiatives to improve export competitiveness and provides actionable insights for policymakers.
 
• **Gujarat**, with its robust industrial base and export-oriented policies, has consistently performed well in the EPI rankings.
 
• The EPI also highlights the role of **district-level export hubs** in promoting local products and contributing to the national export strategy.

questions.question: The natural host of the Nipah Virus is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fruit Bats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **natural host** of the **Nipah Virus (NiV)** is **fruit bats** of the family **Pteropodidae**, particularly those belonging to the genus **Pteropus**.
 
• **Fruit bats** are **reservoir hosts**, meaning the virus naturally exists in these bats without causing them any harm.
 
• The Nipah virus is a **zoonotic virus**, meaning it can spread from animals to humans, and outbreaks have been directly linked to interactions with infected bats or their secretions.
 
• Infected bats can shed the virus in their **saliva, urine, and excreta**, contaminating fruits or other objects that humans or other animals may come in contact with.
 
• Although other animals, such as **pigs**, can act as intermediate hosts, they are not the natural reservoirs of the virus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nipah Virus (NiV):**

 
 
• First identified in **1998** during an outbreak in **Malaysia** and **Singapore**.
 
• The name "Nipah" comes from **Sungai Nipah**, a village in Malaysia where cases were first detected.
 
• It is a member of the **Henipavirus genus** in the family **Paramyxoviridae**.
 
• NiV infection can cause a range of illnesses, from asymptomatic infection to acute respiratory illness and fatal encephalitis.
 
 
 
• **Transmission:**
 
 
• Humans can contract the virus through **direct contact** with infected bats, pigs, or other animals.
 
• Consumption of raw date palm sap contaminated by bat saliva or urine is a common mode of transmission in certain regions.
 
• Human-to-human transmission has also been documented, especially in healthcare settings.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution:**
 
 
• Outbreaks have been reported in **Southeast Asia**, particularly in countries such as **Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, and Singapore**.
 
• **Bangladesh** has faced repeated outbreaks since **2001**, often linked to the consumption of contaminated date palm sap.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms:**
 
 
• Initial symptoms include **fever, headache, and respiratory issues**.
 
• Severe cases may progress to **encephalitis**, causing confusion, seizures, and coma.
 
• The disease has a high fatality rate, ranging from **40% to 75%**, depending on outbreak management and healthcare infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Control:**
 
 
• Avoiding contact with bats and contaminated fruits or sap is crucial for prevention.
 
• Strict infection control measures, including personal protective equipment (PPE), are necessary to prevent human-to-human transmission.
 
• Public health awareness campaigns are vital in high-risk areas to educate people about safe practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Hosts:**

 
 
• **Pigs:** Pigs can act as intermediate hosts, and the 1998 Malaysian outbreak was linked to the transmission of NiV from infected pigs to humans.
 
• **Humans:** Humans are accidental hosts and can contract the virus through direct or indirect contact with infected animals or other humans.
 
 
 
• **Global Concern:**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) has included Nipah virus in its list of **priority diseases** for research and development.
 
• There is no specific treatment or vaccine for Nipah virus, making it a significant public health concern.
 
 
 
• **Recent Outbreaks in India:**
 
 
• In **2018**, Kerala experienced a Nipah virus outbreak that claimed multiple lives.
 
• Since then, Kerala has implemented robust surveillance and response mechanisms to detect and control potential outbreaks.

questions.question: The Gwalior Fort was initiated by ______ who finished the fortification system around the plateau in 773 CE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Sourya Sena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Gwalior Fort** is one of the most significant and historic forts in India, located in **Madhya Pradesh**. It is renowned for its architectural brilliance and historical importance.
 
• The fort was initiated by **Raja Sourya Sena** in **773 CE**. He is credited with laying the foundations of this architectural marvel and establishing its fortification system. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The Gwalior Fort is situated on a **steep sandstone plateau** and has witnessed various rulers and dynasties over the centuries, adding to its rich history and heritage.
 
• Raja Sourya Sena was a ruler who contributed significantly to the early development and defense of the region through this fortification, ensuring the security of his kingdom.
 
• Over time, the fort came under the control of several dynasties, including the **Tomars, Mughals, Marathas, and British**, each leaving their mark on the fort's architecture and history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Architectural Features:**

 
 
• The fort comprises several **palaces, temples, and water tanks**, demonstrating a blend of various architectural styles from different eras.
 
• One of the most famous structures within the fort is the **Man Singh Palace**, built by Tomar king Man Singh in the 15th century. It is renowned for its intricate artwork and tile work.
 
• The **Saas-Bahu Temple** and the **Teli Ka Mandir** are other notable landmarks within the fort, showcasing unique architectural styles.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Gwalior Fort has been a site of numerous battles and power struggles, reflecting the turbulent history of the region.
 
• It was a strategic stronghold due to its location and fortifications, making it a coveted possession for many rulers.
 
• During the Mughal era, the fort served as a prison for political prisoners and royalty.
 
 
 
• **Tourist Attraction:**
 
 
• Today, the Gwalior Fort is a popular tourist destination and is often referred to as the “**Gibraltar of India**” due to its impressive structure and historical significance.
 
• The fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding city and is a UNESCO-recognized monument, attracting history enthusiasts and architecture lovers alike.
 
 
 
• **Other Dynasties:**
 
 
• The fort was later ruled by the **Tomar dynasty**, under whom it saw significant architectural developments.
 
• It also came under the control of the Mughals, particularly during the reign of Babur and Akbar.
 
• The Marathas and later the British also controlled the fort, each adding their own influence to its history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Akbar:**

 
 
• **Mughal emperor Akbar** captured the Gwalior Fort in the 16th century. However, he was not responsible for its initiation or original construction.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga:**
 
 
• **Rana Sanga**, the Rajput ruler of Mewar, was a significant historical figure known for his resistance against the Mughals but had no direct association with the construction of the Gwalior Fort.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• **Ashoka the Great**, the Mauryan emperor, is renowned for his contribution to spreading Buddhism and his edicts, but he was not connected to the Gwalior Fort.

questions.question: "Spao" is a warrior dance performed in which of the following Indian state/Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spao** is a traditional warrior dance performed in the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, India.
 
• This dance is deeply rooted in the cultural and historical traditions of the **Monpas** and other ethnic communities of Ladakh.
 
• The dance symbolizes **valor and bravery**, showcasing the strength and courage of warriors.
 
• Performed during festive occasions and cultural events, the dance is accompanied by traditional Ladakhi music and costumes, which reflect the region’s heritage.
 
• Spao is not only a dance but also a storytelling method that narrates tales of **battles and victories** in Ladakhi history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ladakh:**

 
 
• Ladakh became a Union Territory on **31st October 2019** after the abrogation of Article 370 and the bifurcation of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage, picturesque landscapes, and unique traditions.
 
• The region is home to various ethnic groups like **Monpas, Dards, Bhotias, and Tibetans**.
 
• Traditional dances like Spao and music play a significant role in preserving Ladakhi culture.
 
 
 
• **Other Traditional Dances of Ladakh:**
 
 
• **Shondol:** Known as the royal dance performed during the Ladakhi festivals.
 
• **Yak Dance:** A dance that represents the Yak, an important animal in Ladakhi culture.
 
• **Cham Dance:** A mask dance performed by monks during religious ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Festivals in Ladakh:**
 
 
• Ladakh celebrates unique festivals such as **Losar, Hemis Festival, and Sindhu Darshan**.
 
• These festivals often feature traditional dances like Spao to showcase the region's history and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of Warrior Dances:**
 
 
• Warrior dances are performed to commemorate historical battles and victories.
 
• They emphasize **strength, coordination, and discipline** among performers.
 
• Such dances are often accompanied by traditional instruments like **drums and horns**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Significance:** Ladakh’s unique geography influences its culture, including its dances, music, and festivals.
 
• **Preservation of Heritage:** The Spao dance is a medium to preserve and pass down Ladakhi traditions to future generations.
 
• **Tourism Impact:** Traditional dances like Spao attract tourists, contributing to the region’s economy and cultural awareness.

questions.question: In April 2025, which country has launched the 'Three Gorges Antarctic Eye' telescope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **China** launched the **'Three Gorges Antarctic Eye'** telescope in **April 2025**, marking a significant leap in astronomical research and exploration.

• The telescope is designed for **observing the universe from the Antarctic region**, which is considered one of the best locations for astronomical observations due to minimal atmospheric interference and light pollution.

questions.question: Which IIT launched India's First hyper loop test track in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Madras**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **IIT Madras** launched **India's first hyperloop test track** in **March 2025**, marking a significant milestone in India's transportation innovation landscape. 
• The hyperloop test track was developed under the **Avishkar Hyperloop Project**, a student-led initiative at IIT Madras aimed at developing scalable and sustainable high-speed transportation solutions. 
• The test track is designed to conduct full-scale testing and development of the hyperloop technology, which is a cutting-edge mode of transport capable of achieving speeds up to **1,000 km/h**. 
• Hyperloop is a concept popularized by entrepreneur **Elon Musk**, involving a high-speed train system that operates in near-vacuum tubes, significantly reducing friction and allowing ultra-fast travel. 
• With this launch, India has joined the global race to develop and implement hyperloop technology, putting it on par with countries like the **USA and UAE**, which are also working on similar projects. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **What is Hyperloop Technology?**: 
• Hyperloop is a **high-speed transportation system** involving capsules or pods traveling through a tube with low air pressure. 
• The system uses **magnetic levitation (maglev)** to lift and propel the pods, reducing friction and allowing for rapid speeds. 
• Potential benefits include reduced travel time, energy efficiency, and minimal environmental impact compared to conventional modes of transport. 
• **IIT Madras and the Avishkar Hyperloop Team:** 
• IIT Madras students formed the **Avishkar Hyperloop team** in 2018 to develop indigenous hyperloop technology. 
• The team has actively participated in international competitions, including the **SpaceX Hyperloop Pod Competition**, and has received recognition for their innovative designs. 
• The development of the test track is a significant step toward achieving a functional hyperloop system in India. 
• **Global Context:** 
• Countries like the **United States**, **United Arab Emirates**, and **Canada** are working on hyperloop technology, with several test tracks already operational. 
• The hyperloop concept was first proposed by **Elon Musk** in 2013, and companies like **Virgin Hyperloop** and **Hyperloop Transportation Technologies** are leading the charge in this domain. 
• **Potential Applications:** 
• Hyperloop technology has the potential to revolutionize intercity and interstate travel, making it possible to cover large distances in a matter of minutes. 
• It could also play a significant role in logistics and freight transport, enabling faster delivery times. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Hyperloop vs Traditional Transport:** 
• While traditional high-speed trains can reach speeds of up to **320 km/h**, hyperloop systems can achieve speeds exceeding **1,000 km/h**. 
• Hyperloop is powered by renewable energy sources such as **solar and wind energy**, making it a greener alternative. 
• The cost of building a hyperloop system is projected to be **lower than conventional high-speed rail systems**, but it requires significant initial investment and technological expertise. 
• **Future Prospects in India:** 
• India's hyperloop projects, including the one at IIT Madras, aim to address challenges like traffic congestion and long travel times in densely populated cities. 
• The **Maharashtra government** has also shown interest in developing a hyperloop corridor between **Mumbai and Pune**, reducing the travel time to less than 30 minutes. 
• The success of the test track at IIT Madras could pave the way for large-scale implementation of hyperloop systems in India. </ul

questions.question: When a company hires regular service from external sources which was previously provided internally is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Outsourcing**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Outsourcing** refers to the practice where a company contracts external organizations or service providers to handle tasks, services, or functions that were previously managed internally by its employees. 
• This process is often adopted to improve efficiency, reduce costs, or focus resources on core business activities. 
• Outsourcing is commonly applied to areas like **IT services, customer support, manufacturing, accounting, human resources, and logistics**. 
• It enables organizations to leverage specialized expertise or technology from external vendors while freeing up internal resources. 
• Outsourcing can be implemented domestically (within the same country) or internationally (often referred to as offshore outsourcing). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Subsidization:** 
• Subsidization refers to financial assistance provided by a government or organization to reduce the cost of goods, services, or production for specific groups or industries. 
• It is often employed to support sectors like agriculture, education, renewable energy, or healthcare. 
• Unlike outsourcing, subsidization does not involve delegating tasks to external entities but focuses on monetary aid. 
• Example: Government subsidies for farmers to purchase fertilizers or seeds at reduced costs. 
• **Cross-Subsidization:** 
• Cross-subsidization occurs when revenue from one product, service, or customer group is used to subsidize another product, service, or customer group. 
• This is a common practice in industries like telecommunications, where profits from urban areas may subsidize services in rural areas. 
• It focuses on balancing costs across different segments rather than outsourcing or external contracting. 
• Example: A mobile service provider charging higher rates for premium services to subsidize basic services for low-income users. 
• **Globalization:** 
• Globalization refers to the integration of economies, cultures, and societies across the globe through trade, investment, technology, and information exchange. 
• While outsourcing is a result of globalization, the two are distinct concepts. Globalization is a broader phenomenon, while outsourcing is a business strategy within this framework. 
• Example: Companies setting up manufacturing units in foreign countries to benefit from lower labor costs. 
• Important Points: 
• Outsourcing is driven by factors like cost reduction, access to specialized skills, scalability, and focus on core competencies. 
• It can take various forms, including **offshore outsourcing** (to other countries) and **domestic outsourcing** (within the same country). 
• Challenges of outsourcing include **loss of control, dependency on external vendors, quality concerns, and potential data security risks**. 
• Examples of outsourcing include customer service call centers, IT support, payroll processing, and manufacturing of products like electronic components. 
• Major countries for offshore outsourcing include **India, China, the Philippines, and Eastern Europe**, known for skilled labor at competitive costs. </ul

questions.question: The 1997 ______ Committee Report on Small Enterprises provided the intellectual foundation as well as a practical roadmap for this important reform.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abid Hussain**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **1997 Abid Hussain Committee Report** was a landmark document that provided critical insights into the challenges faced by **small enterprises** in India and proposed reforms to address them. 
• It highlighted the need for a **comprehensive policy framework** to support small enterprises, which play a vital role in the Indian economy by generating employment and contributing to GDP. 
• The committee emphasized the importance of reducing **regulatory bottlenecks** and enhancing access to **credit** for small enterprises, which often struggle due to financial constraints. 
• It also advocated for the promotion of **entrepreneurship development** programs to foster innovation and skill development among small business owners. 
• The recommendations of the Abid Hussain Committee laid the foundation for several policy measures aimed at improving the ecosystem for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Abid Hussain:** 
• Abid Hussain was a **distinguished economist** and a former **Indian diplomat** who made significant contributions to policy-making in India. 
• He served as the **India’s ambassador to the United States** from 1990 to 1992 and held several key positions in the Indian government, including as a member of the **Planning Commission**. 
• His expertise in economics and governance made him a pivotal figure in various committees, including the one on **Small Enterprises**. 
• **Challenges for Small Enterprises:** 
• Small enterprises often face challenges such as **limited access to credit**, high regulatory compliance costs, lack of skilled labor, and inadequate infrastructure. 
• They are also vulnerable to market fluctuations and face stiff competition from larger businesses and multinational corporations. 
• **Policy Reforms Post-1997:** 
• Following the recommendations of the Abid Hussain Committee, the government introduced measures to **simplify registration processes** for small enterprises and improve their access to institutional finance. 
• The establishment of dedicated financial institutions like the **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** was a step in this direction. 
• Programs to promote **technology adoption** and skill development were also launched to enhance the competitiveness of small enterprises. 
• **Comparison of Other Options:** 
• **P. L. Tandon:** Known for the Tandon Committee Report (1974) on working capital management in India, which focused on the banking sector rather than small enterprises. 
• **K. L. Rekhi:** Not associated with major contributions related to small enterprises or policy frameworks. 
• **Abhijit Sen:** An economist known for his work in agriculture and rural development but not related to the 1997 committee on small enterprises.

questions.question: "This sector of economic activities involves processing of new materials derived from primary sector into products for sale or consumption." Which sector of the economy is being talked about in the information given above?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary Sector**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **Secondary Sector** involves the transformation of **raw materials** obtained from the **Primary Sector** into finished goods and products. These goods are further distributed for **consumption or sale**. 
• Examples of activities in the Secondary Sector include **manufacturing, construction, and industrial processing**, such as factories producing goods like automobiles, textiles, and electronics. 
• This sector is often referred to as the **manufacturing sector** due to its role in converting basic materials into usable products. 
• The Secondary Sector adds significant value to raw materials through the processes of **refining, fabricating, and assembling**. For instance, crude oil is refined into petrol, and iron ore is converted into steel. 
• This sector is crucial for economic development as it generates **employment opportunities**, contributes to **export growth**, and drives industrialization. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Primary Sector:** 
• This sector involves the **extraction of natural resources** directly from the earth, such as agriculture, fishing, forestry, and mining. 
• It serves as the foundation for the economy, providing essential **raw materials** for further processing in the Secondary Sector. 
• Examples: Farming crops, harvesting timber, extracting minerals, and fishing. 
• **Tertiary Sector:** 
• Also known as the **service sector**, it focuses on providing **services** rather than goods. 
• Activities include **retail, transportation, healthcare, education, banking, and entertainment**. 
• This sector is vital for ensuring the distribution and consumption of goods produced in the Secondary Sector. 
• **Quaternary Sector:** 
• This sector deals with **knowledge-based activities** such as **research, development, information technology, and education**. 
• It supports innovation and advancement by utilizing data and intellectual expertise. 
• Examples: Scientific research, software development, and higher education services. 
• **Quinary Sector:** 
• This sector includes **high-level decision-making and policy formulation** activities. 
• It is associated with **executive leadership, government officials, and top-level management** in various organizations. 
• Examples: CEOs, government ministers, and heads of international institutions like the United Nations. 
• **Industrial Revolution:** 
• The **Industrial Revolution** in the 18th and 19th centuries marked the beginning of large-scale industrial processing and manufacturing in the Secondary Sector. 
• It led to advancements in **technology, infrastructure, and factory systems**, transforming economies globally. 
• Countries like the UK, USA, Germany, and Japan became industrial powerhouses during this era. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Role in Economic Growth:** 
• The Secondary Sector contributes significantly to a country's **GDP** by adding value to raw materials. 
• It plays a pivotal role in **export-oriented economies**, allowing countries to trade finished goods globally. 
• **Environmental Concerns:** 
• Industrial activities in the Secondary Sector often lead to issues like **pollution, resource depletion, and waste generation**. 
• Sustainable practices and green technologies are being adopted to minimize environmental impact. 
• **Global Examples:** 
• Countries with strong Secondary Sectors include **China** (manufacturing hub), **Germany** (automobile production), and **South Korea** (electronics manufacturing). 
• Emerging economies like **India** are also experiencing growth in this sector, driven by industrialization and urbanization. </ul

questions.question: Rourkela steel plant was established in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1959**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rourkela Steel Plant** was established in the year **1959**, marking a significant milestone in India's industrial development.
 
• It was the first public sector steel plant in India to be set up with the technical collaboration of a foreign country, specifically **Germany**.
 
• Located in **Rourkela**, Odisha, the plant was developed under the second Five-Year Plan to boost the country's steel production capacity.
 
• The plant is operated by the **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)**, one of the largest state-owned steel-making companies in India.
 
• Rourkela Steel Plant played a vital role in driving India's industrial growth by producing high-quality steel for various sectors such as construction, railways, and heavy engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Five-Year Plans and Rourkela Steel Plant:**

 
 
• The establishment of the Rourkela Steel Plant was part of India's **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)**, which focused on industrialization and self-reliance.
 
• The plant was envisioned to support India's growing demand for steel and reduce dependence on imports.
 
 
 
• **Technical Collaboration:**
 
 
• The plant was set up with the technical assistance of the German firms **Krupp** and **Demag**, showcasing India's willingness to adopt advanced technology from abroad.
 
• This collaboration helped in building a strong foundation for India's steel industry.
 
 
 
• **Features of Rourkela Steel Plant:**
 
 
• The plant has advanced facilities for **hot and cold rolling**, as well as a wide range of steel-making processes.
 
• It is equipped to produce a variety of steel products such as **plates, sheets, and structurals**, catering to diverse industrial needs.
 
 
 
• **Importance to Odisha:**
 
 
• The establishment of the Rourkela Steel Plant contributed significantly to the **economic development** of Odisha, creating numerous job opportunities and boosting the state's infrastructure.
 
• It also led to the growth of ancillary industries in the region.
 
 
 
• **Other Major Steel Plants in India:**
 
 
• **Bhilai Steel Plant** in Chhattisgarh, established in 1959 with Soviet collaboration.
 
• **Durgapur Steel Plant** in West Bengal, established in 1959 with British collaboration.
 
• **Bokaro Steel Plant** in Jharkhand, established in 1972 with Soviet collaboration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL):**

 
 
• SAIL is a **Maharatna company** and one of the largest steel producers in India.
 
• It operates major steel plants across India, including Rourkela, Bhilai, Durgapur, Bokaro, and Burnpur.
 
 
 
• **Role in Nation Building:**
 
 
• Rourkela Steel Plant has contributed significantly to India's infrastructure development, including the production of steel for **railways, bridges, and dams**.
 
• It has also supported India's defense sector by supplying specialized steel for **armored vehicles and missile systems**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The plant has not only generated employment but also facilitated the growth of small and medium-scale industries in the region.
 
• It has enhanced India's export potential by producing high-quality steel products for the global market.
